lore_anchors.definition: The immense prison dimension binding powerful beings from across the chaosverse, secured by unbreakable Heavenly Locks that seal the truesoul itself.
The unbreakable chains of the World Prison; bound to the truesoul, not the physical body, making escape impossible.
The cultivation tier above Elder God/Ancestral Immortal; a being with the power to create or destroy an entire Chaosworld.
A Ki Refiner who has reached the World-level by creating a Chaosworld inside their Golden Core.
A Fiendgod who has reached the World-level, possessing the physical might to create a Chaosworld.
The three qualities of a Celestial Immortal's foundation, determined by the method of condensation during the breakthrough from the mortal realm.
An extremely powerful World-level existence and the supreme ruler of the Ninefang Chaosworld.
A precious fluid distilled from chaos, used as a key catalyst for soul-splitting clone techniques.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Ji Ning's combat power far exceed what his lowest-grade Golden Core should allow?
cultural_notes_faq.a: His strength is a combination of two cultivation systems; his monstrous Fiendgod body and high-tier treasures compensate for his weak Ki Refining foundation.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Can Ji Ning fix his low-grade Golden Core now that he's a True Immortal?
cultural_notes_faq.a: No, the dog explicitly states his path is set and he cannot change his foundation.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Are the Ninefang Domain's first-grade Celestial Immortals stronger than Ji Ning?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Pure theory suggests yes, their ki is vaster and purer, but Ji Ning's hybrid combat style makes a direct comparison difficult without a real fight.
